sections.h2: Which Coweta County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three bodies matter to a Coweta County owner: the Tax Commissioner, the Board of Assessors and the Board of Equalization. The Tax Commissioner is at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan, GA 30265, phone 770-254-2670, open Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 4:30pm.

The Assessor's Office is at 37 Perry Street in Newnan, phone 770-254-2680. It values property and decides homestead eligibility. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the grand jury, hears appeals. The Tax Commissioner's site also notes that the Board of County Commissioners and the Board of Education set the millage rates that turn the value into a bill.

  • Questions about value or exemptions: Assessor's Office.
  • Questions about bills, payoffs and liens: Tax Commissioner.
  • A copy of your deed: Clerk of Superior Court, Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan.

sections.h2: What is Coweta County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Coweta County is a West Central Georgia county in the Piedmont and part of Metro Atlanta, with Newnan as its seat and largest city. Wikipedia gives the area as 446 square miles and says the county was laid out in 1826 after the Creek cession and named for the Koweta people.

Newnan, Senoia, Grantville, Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills are cities, and Haralson, Moreland, Sharpsburg and Turin are towns. Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills reach into Fulton County. Shenandoah, a 7,400-acre planned town from the early 1970s, was foreclosed on in 1981, one of the more unusual chapters in local land history.

Growth has been steady: 127,317 residents in 2010, 146,158 in 2020 and 160,240 in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. QuickFacts lists a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied home of $357,500, a 78.4% owner-occupied rate, median gross rent of $1,488 and median household income of $95,548. Mean travel time to work is 29.8 minutes.

sections.h2: What is the Coweta County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Coweta County mails bills on October 1 and the taxes are due December 1. The Tax Commissioner's site says bills go out at least 60 days ahead, and that the due date printed on your bill governs.

If December 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies at the office. Payments by mail need a postmark on or before the due date. The building has a drive-up drop box, and the website accepts card payments with a convenience fee charged by the card company.

  • January 1: ownership and use fixed for the tax year.
  • January 1 to April 1: window to file a return or a homestead application.
  • April 1: mobile and manufactured home taxes due, with a location decal issued after payment.
  • October 1: bills mailed.
  • December 1: real estate and personal property taxes due.

sections.h2: How do penalties and liens work in Coweta County?
sections.html:
After the due date, interest accrues monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%, and a 5% penalty arrives 120 days after the due date and again every 120 days, capped at 20%. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500 is spared the penalty.

A lien called a FiFa is recorded on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court when the bill stays unpaid, and the FAQ places that at more than 30 days past the due date. The office states that a lien remains on a credit record for at least seven years. Because delinquent notices go out only at intervals, the office tells owners to verify the amount due before they pay.

A mobile or manufactured home that misses the April 1 payment faces a 10% penalty, a citation to Coweta County State Court, or possible sale of the home.

sections.h2: Who is responsible for the tax when a Coweta County house is sold?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's guidance is blunt: if you sell, forward the bill to the buyer, but the lien still goes in the name of whoever owned on January 1. The only way to shift it is to prove, within 90 days of the due date, that the buyer is contractually responsible.

That proof is the closing statement. A seller whose closing prorated the tax should deliver a copy to the Tax Commissioner at Newnan Station Drive inside the 90 days. If the office receives it and the bill is still unpaid, the lien can be recorded against the new owner.

Because Coweta County bills are mailed in October, a house that sells in the spring or summer will often close before the year's bill exists. Ask the title company how it is estimating that year's tax at the closing, and ask the Tax Commissioner for last year's total as a reference point.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Coweta County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the assessment notice to file a written appeal with the Board of Assessors. The appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption, and the state supplies a uniform appeal form. In that first filing you must name the method you want.

Three appeal routes listed by the Coweta County Tax Commissioner
RouteWho it fitsOutcome
Board of EqualizationMost ownersHearing, then Superior Court if still unhappy
Hearing officerNon-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or moreDecision, then Superior Court
ArbitrationOwner with a current certified appraisalHearing within 30 days; decision is final

Under the Board of Equalization route, the assessors may change the value and send a new notice, and you then have 30 days to appeal that amended notice. If they do not change it, the appeal goes straight to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.

sections.h2: What homestead and preferential programs apply in Coweta County?
sections.html:
To claim a homestead, you must own and live in the home on January 1, and the application must be received by April 1 of the first year. Late applications roll to the next year. The Assessor's Office makes the final decision, and a denial can be appealed. You may not claim a homestead on any other property in Georgia or another state.

Coweta County has local exemptions that replace the state amount when theirs is larger, and the assessors can give the current list with proof requirements for age, income or military service. Once granted, the exemption renews on its own until you move or the ownership changes.

  • Deferral: qualified owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less may defer tax until the ownership changes or the deferred balance and interest reach 85% of fair market value.
  • Agricultural assessment at 30% of fair market value for qualifying farmland.
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection, with covenants of 10 or 15 years.
  • Historic property and Hazardous Site Reuse preferential assessments.

These special programs must be filed between January 1 and April 1 of the first year claimed. A buyer of an enrolled tract should ask the assessors whether the covenant continues.

faqs.q: When are Coweta County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1, with bills mailed October 1. The Tax Commissioner's site adds that the date printed on your bill controls and that a weekend or holiday moves payment to the next business day.

faqs.q: Where is the Coweta County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan, GA 30265. The phone is 770-254-2670 and the office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 4:30pm.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Coweta County value?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, filed in writing with the Board of Assessors. The filing must name the appeal method you choose.

faqs.q: Does a Coweta County hearing officer hear homestead appeals?
faqs.a: No. The county's description limits hearing officers to disputes over the value of non-homestead real property worth $1,000,000 or more.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my deed in Coweta County?
faqs.a: From the Clerk of Superior Court at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, GA 30263. The Tax Commissioner's FAQ lists the clerk's number as 770-254-2690.
